item.title: George Lucas’ sprawling Skywalker Ranch in California

item.description: A Pennsylvania couple, Tyler and Lauren Bouldin, bought an abandoned stone house at an auction for $460,000. La Comisión Europea sigue el caso “muy de cerca” y mantiene contactos con las autoridades sanitarias europeas, aunque por ahora no existe confirmación de un brote en la región de Irkutsk. item.description: Chryssa Ntalaka’s classroom has become an object lesson in subtraction. item.description: Delano D’Souza is pleased to welcome Dr Shauna Burke, Associate Professor in Exercise and Health Psychology at the University of Leeds. A passionate mountaineer who first summited Mount Everest in 2005, Dr Burke returned to the world’s highest mountain earlier this year, following her diagnosis with stage four breast cancer. She is now setting her sights on the world's 13 other 8,000-metre peaks. For Dr Burke, the mountains are more than a backdrop to an extraordinary personal challenge. “When I’m in the mountains, I do feel at peace. I feel alive,” she says. item.title: Egyptian journalist faces terrorism charges after entire newsroom detained
item.description: Calls for release of six Matsadaash staff after one is charged, while whereabouts of other five remain unknown An Egyptian journalist has been charged with joining a terrorist group, days after an entire newsroom was detained in what rights groups have said is a crackdown on press freedoms. Last week, authorities arrested six journalists from the independent fact-checking and investigative platform Matsadaash – literally meaning “don’t believe” – accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and publishing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Has plague returned to Siberia? Panic in Russia after death of lab worker
item.description: A female staff member at an anti-plague institute in the Irkutsk region who died amid rumours of a "black death" outbreak was diagnosed with "pneumonia of unknown origin". Rospotrebnadzor insists that the situation in the region is "stable". Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: 1,500 Hong Kong residents tour revamped Huanggang Port border crossing
item.description: More than 1,500 Hong Kong residents toured the revamped Huanggang Port border crossing on Sunday as authorities pushed ahead with preparations for its opening. A Security Bureau spokesman said that participants took franchised buses or cross-boundary coaches from various districts to reach the crossing and were shown the new port building in groups. “The event effectively enhanced participants’ understanding of the public transport arrangements, immigration and customs clearance and... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Hotstone Yoga closure losses rise to HK$7.8 million as 694 customers file reports
item.description: Losses linked to the abrupt closure of Hotstone Yoga have risen to nearly HK$8 million (US$1 million), with close to 700 reports filed by affected customers in Hong Kong, according to authorities. The Customs and Excise Department said that as of 6pm on Sunday, it had received 694 reports relating to the yoga chain, involving service contracts worth about HK$7.8 million. The Consumer Council said it had received 416 complaints by 5pm the same day, with claimed losses totalling HK$5.42... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Up to 500 French schools to be totally or partly closed Monday amid student protests
item.description: Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" at up to 500 high schools across France on Monday, the country's education minister has said, after days of sometimes violent protests against teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and overcrowding in classrooms. The minister said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of protests. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Creíamos que lo peor de la peste negra fueron los millones de muertos de la Edad Media. Hubo algo peor: cuatro siglos de oleadas
item.description: La historia de Europa es prolija en guerras, crisis y hambrunas, pero pocos episodios hay tan devastadores como la peste negra , la funesta epidemia que acabó con la vida de millones de personas en la Edad Media. Hay quien calcula que en algunas regiones del continente la mortalidad escaló a niveles aterradores, de casi el 60% . Aunque los historiadores saben desde hace tiempo que la Yersinia pestis causó estragaos entre los siglos XIV y XVIII, el foco suele centrarse en el brote a gran escala registrado entre 1347 y 1353 , la 'muerte negra'. Ahora un estudio nos ha revelado nuevos detalles… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: In 1963, scientist swabbed his daughter’s throat; her virus strain led to a mumps vaccine in 1967
item.description: In 1963, scientist Maurice Hilleman collected a mumps virus sample from his five-year-old daughter Jeryl Lynn. Researchers weakened the virus to develop a vaccine, which was approved in 1967. The vaccine, based on the Jeryl Lynn strain, remains in use and helped transform the fight against mumps in the US. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
